text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — gpu-pool-eu-high-queue triggered (severity: P1). Autoscaler reports repeated scale failures. Affected: hosted inference EU region. Link: https://redwood.incidents/6187654321 :rotating_light:

opsbot: autoscaler error snippet from controller logs:
```
error: scaleup failed: quotaExceeded: unable to create instance (region eu-west-1)
retries=5, last_err=\"quotaExceeded\"
```

sre_jen: I'm on pager. Looking at metrics now — queue length is spiking across all EU pools. Latency SLOs breached for gen endpoints.

infra_paul: I see failed provider responses back to autoscaler (429/503) and our cloud quota for GPU vCPUs is at 98%. Manual provisioning blocked by quota.

maya_ops: @infra_paul can we request emergency quota bump? Who owns the provider ticket?

infra_paul: Opening support ticket with provider now. ETA for quota increase unknown. Raising request as urgent. Ticket: PROV-9012.

samir_ml: Data point: traffic pattern shows sustained 3x increase in long-seq chat workloads since 02:00 UTC. Cache hit-rate dropped because many requests are to new prefixes.

kate_support: We already have customer reports — several enterprise customers seeing 500s and long tail timeouts. CS is pausing new onboarding jobs in EU.

ryan_product: Any safe throttles we can apply to low-priority routes? Need to protect SLAs for Dedicated customers.

sre_jen: Yes — we can enact dynamic route-level throttling for low-tier traffic. I'll push a policy to reject requests >X tokens for free-tier and deprioritize embedding batch jobs.

opsbot: runbook step: POST /ops/route-control throttle-add {\"route\":\"/v1/generate\",\"policy\":\"priority:low,limit:2rps\"} returned 202

maya_ops: Throttles live. Seeing immediate drop in queue ingestion rate. Good stop-gap.

infra_paul: Provider ticket acknowledged. They report capacity reclamation in ~30-60m once approvals processed. Meanwhile, autoscaler keeps failing because cloud API is rate-limiting our pool creation calls.

samir_ml: Can we failover some traffic to a compatible non-EU model (e.g., smaller quantized variant in us-east) as fallback? Need routing changes and latency tradeoffs.

sre_jen: Routing fallback turned on for canary tenants only. We should expand to a broader set while we avoid customer-visible double hop. I will update smart-routing policy to: prefer eu pools, fallback to us-east-quant for tier>=standard.

opsbot: smart-routing update applied to 60% of rollouts.

kate_support: Communicating to affected customers: status.redwood.ai updated with EU capacity issue and mitigations. CS: sending targeted note to enterprise accounts in region.

ryan_product: Important: add a communication note that Dedicated customers unaffected (if true) — avoid unnecessary alarms.

infra_paul: Confirmed Dedicated pools isolated; only shared-hosted eu pools affected.

sre_jen: Quick checklist before handoff: 1) throttles in place 2) routing fallback expanded 3) provider ticket open 4) telemetry dashboards pinned. Anything else?

maya_ops: Adding temporary admission control to embeddings batch queue to stop new bulk jobs (applied).

samir_ml: Suggestion for medium-term: enable prefix-KV caching for heavily repeating chat sessions to reduce token work. I'll spin up an eval to quantify.

infra_paul: Provider says initial quota bump granted for 40 GPUs, but cloud API is still throttling our create calls; they expect steady capacity in ~20 minutes once rps limits lift.

opsbot: autoscaler observed scale operations resuming (partial). Pool growth visible +20 GPUs in eu-west-1. Queue length trending down slowly.

sre_jen: Good. Keep throttles until we hit normal headroom. Monitor tail latency.

kate_support: Customer update drafted and posted. Two large customers reported timeouts earlier; both acknowledged mitigation but ask for root cause once resolved.

maya_ops: Paging to oncall for handoff in 10m. I'll assemble timeline.

opsbot: Handoff to next on-call: @sre_jen -> @infra_paul scheduled at 6187654360.

infra_paul: Taking handoff. Monitoring backend creation metrics; new GPUs are healthy and joining pools. Autoscaler error rate went from 85% -> 12% in last 5m.

samir_ml: Queue and in-flight token consumption now falling. Latency per token back to baseline for most routes.

sre_jen: Marking incident as routing/quotas and autoscaler resilience. We'll keep incident live until stable for 60m.

ryan_product: Postmortem notes to capture: - autoscaler retries vs provider rate-limit behavior - lack of pre-warmed standby capacity in EU - runbook step for emergency quota process - route-level throttling default for free-tier during saturation - communications checklist for large customers.

kate_support: Also add: targeted customer follow-ups + SLA credit evaluation.

opsbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to P2 at 6187654380. Conditions improving.

infra_paul: Provider now shows full API RPS restored. No residual create errors. Autoscaler completed backlog scale in ~12 minutes after lift.

maya_ops: Removing throttles in 5m in a staged fashion.

samir_ml: I will run an analysis on request composition and recommend quantized fallbacks for high-cost model calls.

sre_jen: Preparing immediate action items for postmortem:
- ACTION: infra_paul -> formalize priority quota escalation playbook and contact list (due in 3d)
- ACTION: samir_ml -> eval cache + quantized fallback for EU-hosted heavy workloads (due in 7d)
- ACTION: ops -> add automated throttle policy to runbook when queue growth > threshold (due in 2d)
- ACTION: cs -> customer outreach + SLA assessment (due in 2d)

kate_support: Acknowledged. I'll coordinate outreach and SLA notes.

opsbot: INCIDENT RESOLVE: service metrics stable; closing incident thread at 6187654393. Please create postmortem doc in /docs/incidents once assigned. :white_check_mark:

sre_jen: Thanks everyone. We'll file a detailed postmortem and schedule a retro with infra and ML within next sprint.

maya_ops: Adding timeline artifact to incident doc: stack traces, autoscaler logs, provider ticket link PROV-9012, customer impact summary attached.

samir_ml: adding notes about potential policy to prefer quantized variants automatically during region-saturation events.

ryan_product: Great. Let's make the throttling + fallback configs as a default safety net so we don't need manual toggles next time.

kate_support: I'll follow up with customers after the postmortem is published.

pagerduty-bot: Incident closed. Summary: GPU capacity exhaustion in EU due to provider quota + traffic surge; mitigations: emergency throttles, routing fallback, provider quota bump; action items assigned.
